deck: Table Rock this morning: 910.25 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Streamer on the generate.
play.body: When SWPA spins it, Taneycomo becomes a small river. A dark wooly bugger in the seams.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 910.46 early in the week to 910.21 this morning — about 0.25 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Live USACE reading 14:00 CT: 910.21 ft, 685 cfs through the dam. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At roughly 910.25 ft this morning, the lake is about 4.75 ft below full pool. More shoreline and hazards are exposed in the coves, creek arms (especially James, Kings, and Long Creek), and near some boat ramps — navigate carefully and check conditions before launching.

Surface water has cooled into the low-to-mid 50s°F with outstanding clarity. Bass are hitting topwaters and soft plastics early before transitioning to jigs, live bait, or drop-shot presentations around long points, gravel flats that drop into 20–40 ft, and offshore structure. Walleye are showing on points in 20–25 ft, while crappie and spotted bass hold in deeper brush and around docks. Clean, natural presentations in this clear cooling water continue to produce good catches for anglers dialed into the fall transition.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~685 cfs at 14:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater fishery stays productive year-round thanks to consistent MDC stocking and cold releases from the bottom of Table Rock Dam. Generation remains the primary tactic book: low or no generation allows lighter rigs, wading, or indicator fishing in the seams; stronger flows call for added weight, drifting the current breaks, and 2–4 lb test.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits allowed. Rainbows 12 to 20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, or other soft plastics/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many areas. Recent patterns show solid rainbow numbers with increasing brown activity in the upper stretches. Marabou jigs, midges, scuds, small streamers, and eggs work well. Water clarity is generally excellent. Always call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA generation schedule before heading out and stay clear of the closed zone below the dam.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
